AbstractDB2Dictionary, AbstractMySQLDictionary, AbstractSQLServerDictionary, AccessDictionary, CacheDictionary, EmpressDictionary, FirebirdDictionary, FoxProDictionary, H2Dictionary, HerdDBDictionary, HSQLDictionary, InformixDictionary, IngresDictionary, InterbaseDictionary, JDataStoreDictionary, MaxDBDictionary, OracleDictionary, PointbaseDictionary, PostgresDictionary, SolidDBDictionary
public class DBDictionary extends Object implements Configurable, ConnectionDecorator, JoinSyntaxes, LoggingConnectionDecorator.SQLWarningHandler, IdentifierConfiguration
Class which allows the creation of SQL dynamically, in a database agnostic fashion. Subclass for the nuances of different data stores.

      public boolean allowsBulkTargetInSubselect
      Whether a subquery in the WHERE clause of a bulk update or delete may read the table that the statement changes. When false, the statement matches the primary keys of the affected rows in a derived table instead, which the database materializes before changing any row.

    • supportsMultipleNontransactionalResultSets

      public boolean supportsMultipleNontransactionalResultSets

    • requiresSearchStringEscapeForLike

      public boolean requiresSearchStringEscapeForLike
      Set to true for a database whose LIKE has a default escape character (e.g. backslash). Jakarta Persistence gives a LIKE pattern without an ESCAPE clause no escape character at all, so such a database is given an explicit searchStringNoEscape ESCAPE clause to make the same JPQL query mean the same thing everywhere.

    • searchStringEscape

      public String searchStringEscape

    • searchStringNoEscape

      public String searchStringNoEscape
      The SQL expression written into the ESCAPE clause of a LIKE whose query supplied no escape character, used when requiresSearchStringEscapeForLike is set. The default empty string literal is a non-standard spelling of "no escape character" which H2 and PostgreSQL accept, and MySQL only while its sql_mode has no NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES; a standard conforming database such as Derby rejects it, because the standard wants exactly one character. A dictionary which sets requiresSearchStringEscapeForLike has to make sure that the value is one its database accepts, and otherwise name a single character expression that cannot occur in a pattern.

    • backslashEscapesInStringLiterals

      public boolean backslashEscapesInStringLiterals
      Set to true for a database which may read a backslash inside a string literal as an escape character, such as MySQL and MariaDB unless their sql_mode contains NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, or PostgreSQL with standard_conforming_strings turned off. As that mode can differ between servers and even sessions, a string value with a backslash is then never written into the SQL text as a literal, but bound as a parameter. See toStringLiteral(String).

    • requiresCastForCaseStringResult

      public boolean requiresCastForCaseStringResult
      If true, a string literal, or a parameter bound to a string, returned by a CASE expression is cast to VARCHAR, for databases that type a string literal as CHAR and pad the result of the CASE to the length of its longest result.

    • isConnected

      public boolean isConnected()
      Whether connectedConfiguration(Connection) has run, i.e. whether this dictionary has seen a connection and the settings it derives from the server it is talking to are in place. A dictionary that is chosen from the connection URL alone is not connected until something first asks the configuration for its connection factory.

    • connectedConfiguration

      public void connectedConfiguration(Connection conn) throws SQLException
      This method is called when the dictionary first sees any connection. It is used to initialize dictionary metadata if needed. If you override this method, be sure to call super.connectedConfiguration.
      Throws:
      SQLException

    • configureNamingRules

      protected void configureNamingRules()
      Configures the naming rules for this dictionary. Subclasses should override this method, providing their own naming rules.

    • getNormalizingRule

      protected IdentifierRule getNormalizingRule()
      The rule with which normalize(DBIdentifier) decides whether a name is delimited. Like the default rule of Normalizer it delimits no reserved words, unless a dictionary sets them and switches their delimiting on in configureNamingRules().
      Since:
      4.2.0

    • normalize

      public DBIdentifier normalize(DBIdentifier name)
      Returns the given identifier as it is named for this dictionary. Identifiers are created by Normalizer, which delimits a name that is no valid SQL identifier, but no reserved word, as the reserved words differ from database to database and the rule of Normalizer is shared by all dictionaries of the JVM. If the normalizing rule of this dictionary delimits reserved words, as on MySQL and MariaDB, a name of the identifier that is such a word is delimited, as if the identifier had been created with that rule: it keeps its case, and the names built from it are delimited too. Otherwise the identifier is returned as it is.
      Returns:
      the given identifier, or a delimited copy of it
      Since:
      4.2.0

    • getTimestampPrecision

      public int getTimestampPrecision(Column col)
      The granularity, in nanoseconds, to which a timestamp bound to the given column is rounded. A column whose precision - the number of fractional digits of a second it keeps - is known holds multiples of the corresponding power of ten; otherwise this is datePrecision. Binding a value at the precision the column stores makes a value read back, or kept in memory, compare equal to the stored one, which a timestamp version column depends on.
      Parameters:
      col - the column the value is bound to; may be null
      See Also:
      • Column.getPrecision()

    • isUnsizedDecimal

      protected boolean isUnsizedDecimal(Column col)
      Whether the given column is a NUMERIC or DECIMAL column of a non integral Java type that has no column definition and no precision. Such a column may have a scale. Databases that read an unsized decimal type with scale 0 use this to create a type that keeps the fraction of the value instead.

    • appendSize

      protected String appendSize(Column col, String typeName)
      Helper method to add size properties to the specified type. If present, the string "{0}" will be replaced with the size definition; otherwise the size definition will be appended to the type name. If your database has column types that don't allow size definitions, override this method to return the unaltered type name for columns of those types (or add the type names to the fixedSizeTypeNameSet).

      Some databases support "type modifiers", for example the unsigned "modifier" in MySQL. In these cases the size should go between the type and the "modifier", instead of after the modifier. For example CREATE table FOO ( myint INT (10) UNSIGNED . . .) instead of CREATE table FOO ( myint INT UNSIGNED (10) . . .). Type modifiers should be added to typeModifierSet in subclasses.

    • getDateFractionDigits

      Returns:

      See Also:

    • allowsBulkUpdateOfJoinedTables

      public boolean allowsBulkUpdateOfJoinedTables(Select sel)
      Whether toUpdate(ClassMapping, Select, JDBCStore, Object[], Map) changes a bulk update with the given select in one statement that names the tables of the select under their aliases, so that it can set a column of any of these tables, such as a column of a joined superclass table or of a secondary table. Otherwise the statement only changes the table of the mapping.

    • toTableUpdate

      public SQLBuffer toTableUpdate(Table table, Select sel, JDBCStore store, Object[] params, Map<Path,Value> updates, Map<Column,?> versionUpdates)
      Create an UPDATE statement without a WHERE clause that sets the given fields and version columns, all of which are in the given table. A bulk update that sets columns of several tables, which the database cannot change in one statement, is issued as one such statement per table, restricted by the caller to the primary keys of the matching rows.
      Parameters:
      table - the table to update
      sel - the Select of the bulk update
      store - the current store
      params - the query parameters
      updates - the fields to set, keyed by their paths
      versionUpdates - the values of the version columns to set

    • getDeleteTableContentsSQL

      public String[] getDeleteTableContentsSQL(Table[] tables, Connection conn)
      Create SQL to delete the contents of the specified tables. The default implementation drops all non-deferred RESTRICT foreign key constraints involving the specified tables, issues DELETE statements against the tables, and then adds the dropped constraints back in. Databases with more optimal ways of deleting the contents of several tables should override this method.

    • appendNullsPrecedence

      public void appendNullsPrecedence(SQLBuffer ordering, int nullPrecedence)
      Append the SQL representation of a JPA NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST precedence to an ORDER BY buffer whose last appended term is already &lt;expr&gt; ASC or &lt;expr&gt; DESC.

      Default implementation emits ANSI SQL NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST. Dialects that do not support the ANSI syntax should override this method to emulate the behavior (e.g. using &lt;expr&gt; IS NULL as an auxiliary sort key).

      Parameters:
      ordering - the in-progress ORDER BY buffer
      nullPrecedence - QueryExpressions.NULLS_FIRST or QueryExpressions.NULLS_LAST

    • getValidDefaultTableName

      public DBIdentifier getValidDefaultTableName(DBIdentifier name)
      Make the given default table name valid if the database rejects it, that is if it is neither delimited nor all identifiers are delimited, and it is one of the invalid table words. Such a name is made valid like getValidTableName(DBIdentifier, Schema) does, but without making it unique in the schema, so that the same name is derived whether the table exists already or not. For any other name, including reserved words the database accepts as table names, the given identifier itself is returned.

    • getValidDefaultSequenceName

      public DBIdentifier getValidDefaultSequenceName(DBIdentifier name)
      Make the given default sequence name, the generator name of a sequence generator that names no sequence, valid if the database rejects it, under the same conditions as getValidDefaultTableName(DBIdentifier). Such a name is made valid like getValidSequenceName(DBIdentifier, Schema) does, but without making it unique in the schema. For any other name, including reserved words the database accepts as sequence names, the given identifier itself is returned.

    • makeNameValid

      @Deprecated protected String makeNameValid(String name, NameSet set, int maxLen, int nameType)
      Deprecated.
      Shortens the given name to the given maximum length, then checks that it is not a reserved word. If it is reserved, appends a "0". If the name conflicts with an existing schema component, the last character is replace with '0', then '1', etc. Note that the given max len may be 0 if the database metadata is incomplete.

    • makeNameValid

      protected DBIdentifier makeNameValid(DBIdentifier name, NameSet set, int maxLen, int nameType)
      Shortens the given name to the given maximum length, then checks that it is not a reserved word. If it is reserved, appends a "0". If the name conflicts with an existing schema component, the last character is replace with '0', then '1', etc. Note that the given max len may be 0 if the database metadata is incomplete.

    • makeNameValid

      protected String makeNameValid(String name, NameSet set, int maxLen, int nameType, boolean checkForUniqueness)
      Shortens the given name to the given maximum length, then checks that it is not a reserved word. If it is reserved, appends a "0". If the name conflicts with an existing schema component and uniqueness checking is enabled, the last character is replace with '0', then '1', etc. Note that the given max len may be 0 if the database metadata is incomplete. Note: If the name is delimited, make sure the ending delimiter is not stripped off.

    • getStoredProcedureNameCandidates

      protected List<String> getStoredProcedureNameCandidates(String procedure)
      The names to look up a stored procedure with in the database metadata, in order of preference. Metadata lookups are case sensitive, but the procedure was most likely created with an unquoted name, which the database folded according to its schemaCase: e.g. Derby and Oracle store unquoted names in upper case, PostgreSQL in lower case. Hence the given name is tried as is first, then folded to upper case if this database folds to upper case, then in lower case and finally in upper case.

    • isReplicationConnection

      public boolean isReplicationConnection(Connection conn) throws SQLException
      Whether the given connection is a replication connection, whose driver sends the statements of a read-only connection to a replica. The store keeps such a connection read-only outside of a transaction, so that the reads go to a replica, and makes it writable when a transaction begins. This implementation returns false.
      Parameters:
      conn - a connection of the store, possibly wrapped by OpenJPA's decorators
      Throws:
      SQLException
      Since:
      4.2.0

    • matchErrorState

      protected int matchErrorState(Map<Integer, Set<String>> errorStates, SQLException ex)
      Determine the more appropriate type of store exception by matching the SQL Error State of the the given SQLException to the given Error States categorized by error types. Dictionary subclass can override this method and extract SQLException data to figure out if the exception is recoverable.
      Parameters:
      errorStates - classification of SQL error states by their specific nature. The keys of the map represent one of the constants defined in StoreException. The value corresponding to a key represent the set of SQL Error States representing specific category of database error. This supplied map is sourced from sql-error-state-codes.xml and filtered the error states for the current database.
      ex - original SQL Exception as raised by the database driver.
      Returns:
      A constant indicating the category of error as defined in StoreException.

      • setStoreCharsAsNumbers(boolean)

    • setStoreCharsAsNumbers

      public void setStoreCharsAsNumbers(boolean storeCharsAsNumbers)
      Explicitly configure whether Java char fields are stored in numeric columns rather than as CHAR values. User configuration such as openjpa.jdbc.DBDictionary=postgres(StoreCharsAsNumbers=true) goes through this setter. A value set this way is treated as an explicit user choice: dictionaries that auto-detect a database specific default in connectedConfiguration(Connection) must not override it (see isStoreCharsAsNumbersExplicit()). Programmatic configuration and subclasses should prefer this setter over assigning the public storeCharsAsNumbers field, which dictionaries are free to adjust for the detected database version.

    • toStringLiteral

      public String toStringLiteral(String value)
      Return the given value as a SQL string literal which the database reads back as exactly this value, or null if the value cannot be written as such a literal and has to be bound as a parameter instead. Single quotes are doubled. A value with a backslash is not written as a literal if backslashEscapesInStringLiterals is set, because escaping the backslash would change the value on a server which does not read it as an escape character. A dictionary overrides this method if its database may read other values in a literal differently.

    • toTypedDateTimeLiteral

      protected String toTypedDateTimeLiteral(String escape, int parseType)
      Return the given JDBC escaped date-time literal, such as {ts '...'}, as the SQL standard typed literal DATE '...', TIME '...' or TIMESTAMP '...', or the escape unchanged if it has no quoted value. For drivers that translate the escape into a plain string literal, which has no date-time type in expressions such as COALESCE or CASE.

    • getExtractDateTimeFieldFunction

      public String getExtractDateTimeFieldFunction(DateTimeExtractField extField)
      Return the SQL that extracts the given field from a date or time value, where {1} stands for the value and may occur more than once. By default this is extractDateTimeFieldFunction with {0} replaced by getExtractField(DateTimeExtractField). Override for databases that need a different function per field.

    • getExtractDateTimePartFunction

      public String getExtractDateTimePartFunction(DateTimeExtractPart part)
      Return the SQL that extracts the date or the time part of a date-time value, where {1} stands for the value and may occur more than once, in which case a parameter is bound once for each occurrence. By default the value is cast to DATE or TIME. Override for databases whose DATE type has a time of day or which have no TIME type.
